transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because this whole thing with our kitchen has been going on for almost two years now, and I know how it sounds when I say it out loud, but I’m sure the contractor and a few people on our block have been working together somehow. Quietly, you know, not in some obvious way. But just enough to keep things wrong, to drag it out, to make us look like we don’t know what we’re talking about.

My husband keeps saying, “Look, here are the receipts,” and he’ll show me papers and dates and what was paid, and the contractor always has some excuse about delays or measurements or supplies or whatever it is that week. But the kitchen is still half-wrong, and it’s not just ordinary mistakes. It feels deliberate. Like they know exactly what they’re doing and they think I won’t notice, or they think if they make enough excuses I’ll just give up. I haven’t given up. I can’t, because it’s our home, and I’m tired of being treated like I’m foolish.
Besides these concerns about the contractor, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear the normal things — the house settling, cars outside, people talking when they’re actually there — and sometimes I’ll think I heard something and then it’s the refrigerator or the pipes, you know how old houses are. But voices, like someone speaking to me when nobody’s there? No, that’s not really what this is.

My concern isn’t that I’m hearing things. It’s more what’s actually been happening with the kitchen and the way people act about it. But no, I haven’t noticed voices or sounds that other people don’t hear.

Aside from this situation with the contractor and neighbors, would you say you've generally had a hard time trusting other people—like friends, family, or coworkers—for as long as you can remember, or is this distrust something new and specific to this kitchen situation?

I wouldn’t say I’ve always been like that with everyone, no. I mean, I’m not someone who just blindly trusts people, but I’ve had friends, I’ve dealt with family, coworkers back when I was working, neighbors over the years — normal things. I’m not sitting around thinking everybody is out to get me.

This is specific. It started with this kitchen and how it’s been handled. Nearly two years of this, and it’s not just one little mistake or one delay. It’s the contractor, and I’m sure some people on the block are quietly in on it somehow, because things keep getting kept half-wrong on purpose. And every time I point it out, there’s another excuse — measurements, supplies, timing — and my husband shows me receipts like that’s supposed to settle it, but receipts don’t explain why the kitchen is still wrong.

So no, I don’t think this is some lifelong problem trusting people. I think I’m reacting to what’s been happening right in front of me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, well-systematized, fixed delusional belief of persecution (contractor and neighbors conspiring to sabotage her kitchen renovation) lasting nearly two years. The delusion is non-bizarre, encapsulated to this specific situation, and not accompanied by hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or broader functional decline typical of schizophrenia. She explicitly denies auditory or other hallucinations. She also denies a lifelong pattern of pervasive distrust or suspiciousness across relationships, which argues against paranoid personality disorder, and instead reports this suspicion emerged specifically in the context of the ongoing dispute, consistent with a circumscribed delusional disorder, persecutory type.
